courses.subject: ELA
courses.title: ELA 4
courses.description: Fourth-grade English Language Arts aligned to the California Common Core State Standards and the 2014 ELA/ELD Framework. Students read whole novels (Island of the Blue Dolphins, The Wonderful Wizard of Oz), myths, fables, poetry, drama and informational texts tied to California, and write personal narratives, explanatory reports, opinion essays and a short research report. Every week weaves reading, writing, grammar and conventions, morphology-based word study, and speaking and listening.
courses.framework: California Common Core State Standards for ELA/Literacy; 2014 California ELA/ELD Framework

standards.RL.4.1: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what it says explicitly and when drawing inferences.
standards.RL.4.2: Determine a theme of a story, drama or poem from details in the text; summarize the text.
standards.RL.4.3: Describe in depth a character, setting or event, drawing on specific details (thoughts, words, actions).
standards.RL.4.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases, including those that allude to significant characters in mythology.
standards.RL.4.5: Explain major differences between poems, drama and prose and refer to their structural elements (verse, rhythm, meter, cast, settings, stage directions).
standards.RL.4.6: Compare and contrast the point of view from which different stories are narrated, including first- and third-person.
standards.RL.4.7: Make connections between the text of a story or drama and a visual or oral presentation of it.
standards.RL.4.9: Compare and contrast the treatment of similar themes and patterns of events in stories, myths and traditional literature from different cultures.
standards.RL.4.10: Read and comprehend grade 4-5 literature proficiently.
standards.RI.4.1: Refer to details and examples in an informational text when explaining what it says and drawing inferences.
standards.RI.4.2: Determine the main idea of a text and explain how it is supported by key details; summarize.
standards.RI.4.3: Explain events, procedures, ideas or concepts in a historical, scientific or technical text, including what happened and why.
standards.RI.4.4: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words in a grade 4 text.
standards.RI.4.5: Describe the overall structure (chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events, ideas or information in a text.
standards.RI.4.6: Compare and contrast a firsthand and secondhand account of the same event or topic.
standards.RI.4.7: Interpret information presented visually, orally or quantitatively (charts, graphs, diagrams, timelines) and explain how it contributes to understanding.
standards.RI.4.8: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text.
standards.RI.4.9: Integrate information from two texts on the same topic to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably.
standards.RI.4.10: Read and comprehend grade 4-5 informational texts proficiently.
standards.RF.4.3: Use combined knowledge of letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns and morphology (roots and affixes) to read unfamiliar multisyllabic words.
standards.RF.4.4: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
standards.W.4.1: Write opinion pieces supporting a point of view with reasons and information.
standards.W.4.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas clearly.
standards.W.4.3: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences using technique, descriptive details and clear event sequences.
standards.W.4.4: Produce clear and coherent writing appropriate to task, purpose and audience.
standards.W.4.5: With guidance, develop and strengthen writing by planning, revising and editing.
standards.W.4.6: With guidance, use technology to produce and publish writing; type a minimum of one page in a single sitting.
standards.W.4.7: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.
standards.W.4.8: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather information from print and digital sources; take notes, categorize and list sources.
standards.W.4.9: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection and research.
standards.W.4.10: Write routinely over extended and shorter time frames for a range of tasks and purposes.
standards.SL.4.1: Engage effectively in collaborative discussions, building on others' ideas and expressing one's own clearly.
standards.SL.4.2: Paraphrase portions of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats.
standards.SL.4.3: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points.
standards.SL.4.4: Report on a topic or text, tell a story or recount an experience in an organized manner with appropriate facts and details; speak clearly at an understandable pace.
standards.SL.4.5: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations to enhance main ideas or themes.
standards.SL.4.6: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English and informal discourse.
standards.L.4.1: Demonstrate command of grammar and usage: relative pronouns and adverbs, progressive verb tenses, modal auxiliaries, adjective order, prepositional phrases, complete sentences, frequently confused words.
standards.L.4.2: Demonstrate command of capitalization, punctuation (commas, quotation marks) and spelling.
standards.L.4.3: Use knowledge of language and its conventions: choose precise words and punctuation for effect.
standards.L.4.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown words using context, Greek and Latin affixes and roots, and reference materials.
standards.L.4.5: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships and nuances (similes, metaphors, idioms, adages, proverbs, antonyms, synonyms).
standards.L.4.6: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases.

units.title: Launching Readers & Writers: Story Elements and Personal Narrative
units.big_idea: Readers notice how characters, settings and events work together; writers shape real experiences into stories.

units.title: Myths, Fables & Traditional Tales
units.big_idea: Stories from many cultures share themes and patterns, and mythology lives on in our language.

units.title: Reading to Learn: Informational Text and Explanatory Writing
units.big_idea: Authors organize information in structures; writers explain a topic clearly with facts and details.

units.title: Novel Study: Island of the Blue Dolphins
units.big_idea: Survival tests and reveals character; fiction and nonfiction together tell a fuller story.

units.title: Poetry & Drama
units.big_idea: Poets and playwrights use structure, sound and figurative language to create meaning.

units.title: Opinion and Argument
units.big_idea: Strong opinions rest on reasons supported by evidence.

units.title: Novel Study: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
units.big_idea: Journeys change characters, and a story can be retold through film, stage and art.

units.title: Research and Report: California Natural Wonders
units.big_idea: Researchers gather, compare and integrate sources, including firsthand accounts, to build knowledge.

units.title: Reflection, Fluency & Portfolio
units.big_idea: Readers and writers reflect on growth and set goals.

weeks.topic: Story elements in Just So Stories
objectives: Identify characters, setting, problem and resolution

days.title: Reading inventory
days.work: Complete a reading interest survey, choose an independent library book, and do a 1-minute fluency read of a grade 4 passage to set a baseline.

days.title: How the Whale Got His Throat
days.work: Read Kipling's 'How the Whale Got His Throat' aloud and fill in a story map with character, setting, problem and solution.

days.title: Details as evidence
days.work: Reread 'How the Camel Got His Hump' and answer 4 questions citing a detail from the text for each.

days.title: Writer's notebook launch
days.work: Make a 'heart map' of memories in the writer's notebook and quick-write for 10 minutes about one memory.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Discuss the two stories with a parent using sentence stems ('I agree because...'), then answer a short story-element check.

weeks.assessment: Story map, cited answers and fluency baseline.

objectives: Describe a character using thoughts, words and actions

days.title: Character traits
days.work: Read 'The Elephant's Child' and chart the Elephant's Child's traits with evidence from his words and actions.

days.title: Prefixes un-, re-, dis-
days.work: Sort 20 words by prefix, define each using the prefix meaning, and use 5 in sentences.

days.title: Narrative planning
days.work: Choose a small moment from the heart map and plan it on a story mountain (beginning, rising events, high point, ending).

days.title: Complete sentences
days.work: Fix 12 fragments and run-ons, then check the narrative plan's first sentences for completeness.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draft the narrative's opening scene with a hook and share it aloud; take a quiz on prefixes and sentence types.

weeks.topic: Drafting narratives with dialogue and detail
objectives: Use dialogue and description to develop events

days.title: Mentor text study
days.work: Reread 'How the Leopard Got His Spots' and highlight dialogue and description; note how Kipling shows feelings.

days.title: Draft the middle
days.work: Draft the narrative's middle events using at least two time-order transitions.

days.title: Quotation marks
days.work: Practice punctuating dialogue in 10 sentences and add 3 lines of dialogue to the draft.

days.title: Show, don't tell
days.work: Rewrite 4 'telling' sentences as 'showing' sentences with sensory details and revise one draft paragraph.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draft the ending and do a timed fluency read of a passage from the independent book.

objectives: Determine a theme and summarize a story

days.title: Theme
days.work: Read 'The Cat That Walked by Himself' and determine a theme supported by two details; write a 5-sentence summary.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise the narrative using a checklist: strong lead, clear sequence, dialogue, satisfying ending.

days.title: Edit
days.work: Edit for capitals, commas, quotation marks and spelling with a parent conference.

days.title: Publish
days.work: Type the final narrative (at least one page) and add a title.

days.title: Celebrate & assess
days.work: Read the narrative aloud to family; take the Unit 1 reading check on a new Just So story.

weeks.assessment: Published personal narrative (rubric) and Unit 1 reading check.

objectives: Determine themes and morals of fables

days.title: Fable reading
days.work: Read 6 Aesop fables (e.g., 'The Ant and the Grasshopper', 'The Fox and the Grapes') and state each moral in your own words.

days.title: Adages & proverbs
days.work: Match 12 adages ('Don't count your chickens...') to meanings and to the fable that fits.

days.title: Suffixes -ful, -less, -ness
days.work: Build and define 15 words with suffixes; note how suffixes change part of speech.

days.title: Discussion
days.work: Discuss with a parent whether the grasshopper deserved help, citing the text.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an original 1-paragraph fable with a moral; quiz on suffixes.

objectives: Explain words that allude to mythology
materials: A Wonder-Book for Girls and Boys (Hawthorne, Gutenberg) or D'Aulaires' Book of Greek Myths (library)

days.title: The Golden Touch
days.work: Read Hawthorne's 'The Golden Touch' (King Midas) and summarize it in a 5-box comic strip.

days.title: Pandora
days.work: Read 'The Paradise of Children' (Pandora) and determine its theme.

days.title: Allusions
days.work: Explain 8 mythological allusions (Midas touch, Pandora's box, Achilles' heel, Herculean) and use 4 in sentences.

days.title: Greek roots
days.work: Learn roots tele, photo, graph, micro, scope and build 12 words.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on allusions and Greek roots; 1-minute fluency read of a myth passage.

weeks.topic: Coyote and trickster tales across cultures
objectives: Compare themes and patterns in tales from different cultures
materials: California Indian Coyote stories (library collection, e.g., Coyote tales)

days.title: Coyote tales
days.work: Read a California Native Coyote story (e.g., how Coyote brought fire) and identify the trickster pattern.

days.title: Anansi
days.work: Read an Anansi tale from West Africa and record its events and theme.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Complete a Venn diagram comparing the two tricksters' themes and patterns of events.

days.title: Point of view
days.work: Rewrite a short scene of the Coyote story in first person as Coyote and discuss what changes.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a compare/contrast paragraph about the two tales citing details.

objectives: Write a narrative explaining a natural phenomenon

days.title: Plan a myth
days.work: Choose a California phenomenon (fog over the Golden Gate, Half Dome's shape) and plan an origin myth.

days.title: Relative pronouns
days.work: Combine sentences using who, whose, which, that, where, when, why (12 items).

days.title: Draft
days.work: Draft the myth with a hero, a problem and an explanation of the phenomenon.

days.title: Revise & edit
days.work: Revise to add at least two relative clauses and edit with a checklist.

days.title: Storytelling & assessment
days.work: Tell the myth aloud as a storyteller; take the Unit 2 test on theme, allusions and comparison.

objectives: Determine main idea and supporting details
materials: ReadWorks grade 4 passages on California animals

days.title: Main idea
days.work: Read a ReadWorks passage on sea otters and state the main idea with three key details.

days.title: Summarize
days.work: Write a 4-sentence summary of a passage on California condors without opinions.

days.title: Domain vocabulary
days.work: Use context and glossaries to define 10 science words from the passages.

days.title: Latin roots
days.work: Learn roots port, rupt, struct, dict and build 12 words.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Read a new passage and write main idea, details and summary independently.

objectives: Identify chronology, comparison, cause/effect and problem/solution

days.title: Chronology
days.work: Read an article on the building of the Golden Gate Bridge and make a timeline.

days.title: Cause/effect
days.work: Read about the 1906 San Francisco earthquake and chart causes and effects.

days.title: Compare/problem-solution
days.work: Read about drought solutions and record the problem and solutions; compare two animals in another passage.

days.title: Structure sort
days.work: Identify the structure of 6 short paragraphs by their signal words.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: name the structure of 4 passages and draw the matching organizer.

materials: nonfiction books on a California animal

days.title: Text features
days.work: Interpret a diagram, a map and a chart in a nonfiction book and explain what each adds.

days.title: Choose a topic
days.work: Choose a California animal for an explanatory report and generate research questions.

days.title: Note-taking
days.work: Take paraphrased notes on note cards from two sources, listing each source.

days.title: Progressive tenses
days.work: Practice past, present and future progressive verbs in 12 sentences about the animal.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Paraphrase a 2-minute video segment aloud and sort notes into categories.

objectives: Write an informative text with headings, facts and a conclusion

days.title: Organize
days.work: Arrange notes into an outline with an introduction, 3 headed sections and a conclusion.

days.title: Draft sections
days.work: Draft the introduction and two sections using linking words (also, for example, because).

days.title: Finish draft
days.work: Draft the last section and conclusion; add one diagram with a caption.

days.title: Revise & publish
days.work: Revise for precise vocabulary, edit, and type the final report.

days.title: Present & assess
days.work: Present the report to family; take the Unit 3 informational reading test.

weeks.topic: Island of the Blue Dolphins, chapters 1-6
objectives: Describe the setting and its effect on characters
materials: Island of the Blue Dolphins (Scott O'Dell, library)

days.title: Setting
days.work: Read chapters 1-2 and map San Nicolas Island; describe how the setting shapes the people's lives.

days.title: Inferences
days.work: Read chapters 3-4 and write 3 inferences about Captain Orlov using text evidence.

days.title: Conflict
days.work: Read chapters 5-6 and discuss the battle and departure with a parent.

days.title: Word study
days.work: Practice syllabication of 15 multisyllabic words from the novel.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer 6 text-dependent questions on chapters 1-6.

weeks.topic: Island of the Blue Dolphins, chapters 7-14

days.title: Alone
days.work: Read chapters 7-9 and chart Karana's actions and feelings after Ramo's death.

days.title: Point of view
days.work: Discuss how first-person narration affects what we know; rewrite a paragraph in third person.

days.title: Building a home
days.work: Read chapters 10-12 and list the survival decisions Karana makes.

days.title: Figurative language
days.work: Find 5 similes/metaphors in chapters 13-14 and explain them.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph on how Karana has changed so far, with two quotes.

weeks.topic: Island of the Blue Dolphins, chapters 15-22

days.title: Rontu
days.work: Read chapters 15-17 and analyze how Karana's relationship with Rontu reveals her values.

days.title: Context clues
days.work: Use context to define 10 words from chapters 18-19.

days.title: Tutok
days.work: Read chapters 18-20 and discuss friendship across conflict.

days.title: Theme
days.work: Read chapters 21-22 and draft a theme statement with supporting details.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer comprehension questions and share the theme statement aloud.

weeks.topic: Island of the Blue Dolphins, chapters 23-29

days.title: Chapters 23-25
days.work: Read and track how Karana's attitude toward animals changes.

days.title: Chapters 26-29
days.work: Finish the novel and discuss whether the ending is happy, sad or both.

days.title: Summary
days.work: Write a one-paragraph summary of the whole novel.

days.title: Fluency
days.work: Rehearse and record a 2-minute expressive reading of a favorite passage.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take the novel comprehension test.

weeks.topic: Fiction meets fact: the Lone Woman of San Nicolas
objectives: Integrate information from novel and nonfiction
materials: nonfiction article on Juana Maria (library/ReadWorks or National Park Service Channel Islands)

days.title: Nonfiction
days.work: Read a nonfiction account of the Lone Woman of San Nicolas Island (Juana Maria) and take notes.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Make a two-column chart of what is historical fact and what Scott O'Dell invented, citing the novel and the article for each row.

days.title: Essay plan
days.work: Plan an essay: 'How does Karana survive, and what does it show about her?'

days.title: Draft & revise
days.work: Draft and revise the essay with at least 3 quotations.

days.title: Present & assess
days.work: Share the essay in a book talk; scored with the literary essay rubric.

objectives: Identify verse, rhythm, meter and rhyme
materials: A Child's Garden of Verses (Stevenson, Gutenberg)
'Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening' (Frost)

days.title: Stevenson
days.work: Read 'My Shadow' and 'The Land of Counterpane'; mark rhyme scheme and count beats.

days.title: Imagery
days.work: Read Sandburg's 'Fog' and explain the extended metaphor.

days.title: Frost
days.work: Read 'Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening' and discuss mood and repetition.

days.title: Write poems
days.work: Write a metaphor poem and a rhyming quatrain about a California place.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Memorize and recite a poem; quiz on poetry terms.

objectives: Connect a poem to an oral presentation

days.title: Paul Revere's Ride
days.work: Read Longfellow's poem and summarize the events stanza by stanza.

days.title: Compare to audio
days.work: Listen to a recorded reading and note how the reader's pacing changes the effect.

days.title: Fact vs poem
days.work: Read a short factual account and list what Longfellow changed.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse 3 stanzas with expression and record them.

days.title: Perform
days.work: Perform with a background sound effect or slides; self-evaluate fluency.

weeks.topic: Drama: reading and performing a play
objectives: Identify drama structure (cast, scenes, stage directions)
materials: reader's theater script of an Aesop fable or 'The Emperor's New Clothes'

days.title: Drama structure
days.work: Read a reader's theater script and label cast list, scenes and stage directions.

days.title: Prose vs drama
days.work: Compare the script to the prose version and list structural differences.

days.title: Write a scene
days.work: Convert a scene from Island of the Blue Dolphins into a short script.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse the script with family members using expression and blocking.

days.title: Perform & assess
days.work: Perform the play; take the Unit 5 test on poetry and drama structure.

weeks.topic: Reasons and evidence in opinion texts
objectives: Explain how authors use reasons and evidence
materials: opinion articles from CommonLit or newspaper kids' sections

days.title: Fact vs opinion
days.work: Sort 15 statements about California (e.g., 'Yosemite is the best park') into fact and opinion and underline the clue words.

days.title: Reasons
days.work: Read an opinion article on school uniforms and outline its reasons and evidence.

days.title: Evaluate evidence
days.work: Rate each piece of evidence as strong or weak and explain.

days.title: Listen for reasons
days.work: Watch a short persuasive video and record the speaker's reasons.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Read a new opinion article independently and fill in an organizer listing the author's claim, three reasons and the evidence for each.

objectives: Introduce an opinion and group reasons

days.title: Choose a topic
days.work: Choose a question (Should California ban single-use plastic bags?) and state an opinion.

days.title: Gather evidence
days.work: Gather facts from two short articles and record them with sources.

days.title: Modal auxiliaries
days.work: Practice can, may, must, should in 12 sentences.

days.title: Outline
days.work: Plan the essay: introduction, 3 reasons with evidence, conclusion.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Debate the topic with a parent arguing the opposite side.

weeks.topic: Drafting and revising the opinion essay
objectives: Link opinion and reasons with words and phrases

days.title: Introduction
days.work: Draft an introduction with a hook and clear opinion statement.

days.title: Body
days.work: Draft three body paragraphs, each with a reason, two pieces of evidence and a linking phrase (for instance, in addition, because).

days.title: Conclusion
days.work: Draft a conclusion that restates the opinion and calls readers to action.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise for precise words and varied sentences.

days.title: Peer conference
days.work: Conference with a parent using the opinion rubric and plan edits.

weeks.topic: Publishing and speaking: formal vs informal

days.title: Edit
days.work: Edit for commas in compound sentences, spelling and capitalization.

days.title: Publish
days.work: Type the final opinion essay in one sitting, formatting the title and paragraphs, and proofread it once aloud.

days.title: Formal vs informal
days.work: Compare a text message and a speech on the same topic and rewrite informal sentences formally.

days.title: Speech
days.work: Turn the essay into a 2-minute speech on note cards and rehearse.

days.title: Deliver & assess
days.work: Deliver the 2-minute speech to family, then take the Unit 6 test on reasons and evidence and opinion writing.

weeks.assessment: Published essay, speech and Unit 6 test.

materials: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (L. Frank Baum, Gutenberg)

days.title: Kansas vs Oz
days.work: Read chapters 1-2 and contrast the settings with details.

days.title: Scarecrow
days.work: Read chapters 3-4 and describe the Scarecrow's traits.

days.title: Tin Woodman
days.work: Read chapters 5-6 and describe the Tin Woodman and Cowardly Lion.

days.title: Prediction
days.work: Write predictions about what the Wizard will grant each character.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer comprehension questions on chapters 1-6.

days.title: The journey
days.work: Read chapters 7-9 and track obstacles and how friends solve them.

days.title: Idioms
days.work: Learn 12 idioms and write a short dialogue for the characters using four.

days.title: The Emerald City
days.work: Read chapters 10-11 and discuss the Wizard's demands.

days.title: Wicked Witch
days.work: Read chapter 12 and describe the turning point.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz explaining 6 idioms and answering text-dependent questions on chapters 7-12.

days.title: Rescue
days.work: Read chapters 13-14 and note each friend's contribution.

days.title: The Wizard revealed
days.work: Read chapters 15-16 and discuss what the Wizard really is.

days.title: Gifts
days.work: Read chapters 17-18 and analyze whether the friends already had what they wanted.

days.title: Theme
days.work: Write a paragraph stating a theme (e.g., 'what you seek may already be inside you') supported by two quotations.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Discuss the theme with a parent and revise the paragraph.

objectives: Compare text with a film version
materials: The Wizard of Oz (1939 film, library DVD)

days.title: Finish
days.work: Read chapters 19-24 (the journey to Glinda) and write a 5-sentence summary of how Dorothy gets home.

days.title: Film
days.work: Watch selected scenes of the 1939 film and note differences (silver shoes vs ruby slippers).

days.title: Compare chart
days.work: Complete a book-vs-film comparison chart covering characters, events, setting colors and the ending.

days.title: Opinion
days.work: Write a paragraph: which version tells the story better and why?

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take the novel comprehension test.

days.title: Compare quests
days.work: Read chapter 1 of Alice's Adventures in Wonderland and compare its journey pattern with Oz.

days.title: Plan
days.work: Plan a new adventure for Dorothy in a California setting.

days.title: Draft
days.work: Draft the episode with dialogue and description.

days.title: Revise & edit
days.work: Revise the episode with the narrative checklist (hook, dialogue, sensory details, ending) and edit for quotation marks.

days.title: Share & assess
days.work: Read the episode aloud; scored with the narrative rubric.

days.title: Choose a wonder
days.work: Choose a California natural wonder (Yosemite, Death Valley, redwoods, Lake Tahoe) and write research questions.

days.title: Credible sources
days.work: Evaluate 4 websites about your topic (.gov, .edu, a museum, a personal blog) for author, date and purpose, and rate each.

days.title: Gather
days.work: Find 3 sources including one with maps or charts.

days.title: Notes
days.work: Take paraphrased notes on note cards with source info.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Check sources and notes with a parent and fix gaps.

materials: John Muir excerpt from 'The Yosemite' or 'My First Summer in the Sierra' (Gutenberg)

days.title: Firsthand
days.work: Read a John Muir excerpt about Yosemite and note what he saw and felt.

days.title: Secondhand
days.work: Read an encyclopedia article on Yosemite and note its focus.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Complete a chart comparing the two accounts' focus and information.

days.title: Integrate
days.work: Write a paragraph integrating information from both.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz identifying firsthand vs secondhand accounts.

days.title: Outline
days.work: Outline the report with an introduction, 3-4 sections and conclusion.

days.title: Draft intro
days.work: Draft an introduction that hooks the reader with a surprising fact, then draft the first headed section from note cards.

days.title: Draft body
days.work: Draft the remaining 2-3 headed sections, paraphrasing notes and including one short quotation with its source.

days.title: Commas
days.work: Practice commas in series and introductory phrases; apply to the draft.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write the conclusion and a source list (title, author, website or publisher) in a consistent format.

days.title: Revise for clarity
days.work: Reread the draft aloud, mark confusing sentences, and revise each section so its first sentence states the section's main idea.

days.title: Edit conventions
days.work: Edit for capitalization of proper nouns (Sierra Nevada, Mojave Desert), commas and spelling using a checklist and dictionary.

days.title: Visuals
days.work: Add a labeled map of the wonder's location and two captioned images, and explain in the caption what each shows.

days.title: Publish
days.work: Type and print the final report with headings, visuals and a source list in a consistent format.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Self-assess the report against the research rubric and write two sentences on its strongest and weakest parts.

days.title: Plan presentation
days.work: Turn the report into 5 slides or a poster, using one key fact and one visual per section.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse the 3-minute talk with a timer, practicing eye contact, volume and pace.

days.title: Audio

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Math 4
courses.description: Fourth-grade mathematics aligned to the California Common Core State Standards. Students extend place value to 1,000,000, become fluent with multi-digit addition and subtraction, multiply up to four digits by one digit and two digits by two digits, and divide with remainders. The heart of the year is fractions (equivalence, comparison, adding/subtracting like denominators, multiplying a fraction by a whole number) and decimal notation, followed by measurement conversion, angle measurement and classification of two-dimensional figures.
courses.framework: California Common Core State Standards for Mathematics; 2023 CA Mathematics Framework

standards.4.OA.A.2: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison.

units.title: Place Value to One Million
units.big_idea: Each place is ten times the place to its right, which lets us read, compare and round big numbers.

units.title: Multi-Digit Addition & Subtraction
units.big_idea: The standard algorithm is place value regrouping written efficiently.

units.title: Multiplication: Comparison, Factors & Multi-Digit
units.big_idea: Multiplication can compare quantities and is built from place-value partial products.

units.title: Division with Remainders
units.big_idea: Division shares or groups by place value; remainders must be interpreted in context.

units.title: Fraction Equivalence & Comparison
units.big_idea: The same amount can be named by many fractions; size depends on numerator and denominator together.

units.title: Fraction Operations
units.big_idea: Fractions are built from unit fractions, so we can add, subtract and multiply them by whole numbers.

units.title: Decimal Fractions
units.big_idea: Tenths and hundredths extend place value to the right of the ones.

units.title: Measurement, Area & Perimeter
units.big_idea: Larger units can be expressed in smaller units, and formulas describe area and perimeter.

units.title: Angles & Two-Dimensional Geometry
units.big_idea: Angles are measured in degrees and help us classify shapes.

units.title: Patterns & Year in Review
units.big_idea: Rules generate patterns, and the year's skills combine to solve multistep problems.

courses.subject: SCI
courses.title: Science 4
courses.description: Fourth-grade science built on the California Next Generation Science Standards and the 2016 CA Science Framework. Students investigate energy (speed, collisions, circuits, sound, light and heat), waves and information transfer, how plant and animal structures support survival and sensing, how weathering, erosion and rock layers record Earth's history, how maps reveal patterns of earthquakes and volcanoes, and how humans use natural resources and reduce hazard impacts. Each week includes a hands-on investigation with household materials and a science notebook entry.
courses.framework: California Next Generation Science Standards (CA NGSS); 2016 California Science Framework

standards.4-PS3-1: Use evidence to construct an explanation relating the speed of an object to the energy of that object.
standards.4-PS3-2: Make observations to provide evidence that energy can be transferred from place to place by sound, light, heat and electric currents.
standards.4-PS3-3: Ask questions and predict outcomes about the changes in energy that occur when objects collide.
standards.4-PS3-4: Apply scientific ideas to design, test and refine a device that converts energy from one form to another.
standards.4-PS4-1: Develop a model of waves to describe patterns in terms of amplitude and wavelength and that waves can cause objects to move.
standards.4-PS4-2: Develop a model to describe that light reflecting from objects and entering the eye allows objects to be seen.
standards.4-PS4-3: Generate and compare multiple solutions that use patterns to transfer information.
standards.4-LS1-1: Construct an argument that plants and animals have internal and external structures that support survival, growth, behavior and reproduction.
standards.4-LS1-2: Use a model to describe that animals receive different types of information through their senses, process it in the brain and respond.
standards.4-ESS1-1: Identify evidence from patterns in rock formations and fossils in rock layers to support an explanation for changes in a landscape over time.
standards.4-ESS2-1: Make observations and/or measurements to provide evidence of the effects of weathering or the rate of erosion by water, ice, wind or vegetation.
standards.4-ESS2-2: Analyze and interpret data from maps to describe patterns of Earth's features.
standards.4-ESS3-1: Obtain and combine information to describe that energy and fuels are derived from natural resources and their uses affect the environment.
standards.4-ESS3-2: Generate and compare multiple solutions to reduce the impacts of natural Earth processes on humans.
standards.3-5-ETS1-1: Define a simple design problem reflecting a need or want, including criteria for success and constraints on materials, time or cost.
standards.3-5-ETS1-2: Generate and compare multiple possible solutions to a problem based on how well each meets the criteria and constraints.
standards.3-5-ETS1-3: Plan and carry out fair tests in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify aspects of a model or prototype that can be improved.

courses.subject: HSS
courses.title: California, A Changing State
courses.description: Grade 4 History-Social Science follows the California History-Social Science Content Standards and the 2016 HSS Framework. Students study California's geography and regions, the diverse nations of California Indians, Spanish exploration and the mission system from multiple perspectives, Mexican California and the ranchos, the Bear Flag Revolt and Mexican-American War, the Gold Rush and statehood, and California's growth into an agricultural, industrial and cultural power, ending with how local, state and federal governments work. Primary sources from Calisphere's curated sets, the Online Archive of California and the Library of Congress anchor every unit.
courses.framework: California History-Social Science Content Standards (Grade 4: California, A Changing State); 2016 California History-Social Science Framework

units.title: The Geography of California
units.big_idea: California's location, regions and physical features shape where and how people live.

units.title: California's First Peoples
units.big_idea: Diverse California Indian nations adapted to and shaped many environments and continue as living communities today.

units.title: Exploration by Land and Sea
units.big_idea: Competing empires explored the North Pacific coast for trade, wealth and territory.

units.title: Missions, Presidios and Pueblos
units.big_idea: Spanish colonization brought soldiers, missionaries and settlers whose institutions transformed Native lives, land and economy.

units.title: Mexican California and the Ranchos
units.big_idea: Mexican independence secularized the missions and created a rancho society built on land grants and Native labor.

units.title: Trails West and the Bear Flag Revolt
units.big_idea: Overland migrants and the Mexican-American War brought California under U.S. control.

units.title: The Gold Rush
units.big_idea: The discovery of gold rapidly transformed California's population, economy, environment and people's lives.

units.title: Statehood
units.big_idea: California became the 31st state with a constitution and government unlike the Spanish and Mexican systems.

units.title: Connecting California: Transportation and Immigration
units.big_idea: Railroads and telegraphs tied California to the nation while immigrants built the state amid conflict and cooperation.

units.title: Modern California: Water, Work and Culture
units.big_idea: Water projects, new industries, schools and artists made California a national leader through hard times and war.

units.title: Governing California
units.big_idea: Federal, state and local governments share power through written constitutions.

days.work: Read about shipyards in Richmond, aircraft factories and women workers using the Calisphere set 'Life on the Home Front During World War II'.

days.title: Japanese American incarceration
days.work: Read about Executive Order 9066 and analyze photos from the Calisphere set 'Japanese American Internment'.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph on how one of these events changed California.

objectives: Trace the growth of public education

days.title: Industries map
days.work: Map aerospace (Southern California), electronics (Silicon Valley), agriculture (Central Valley) and Pacific trade ports.

days.title: Public education
days.work: Read about California's schools, community colleges, CSU and UC systems and the 1960 Master Plan.

days.title: Artists
days.work: Study Ansel Adams' Yosemite photos, read about John Steinbeck and Dorothea Lange, and discuss their impact.

days.title: Entertainment
days.work: Read about Hollywood and Walt Disney and how film spread California culture.

days.title: Unit 10 test
days.work: Take the Unit 10 test on water projects, the Depression and WWII, industries, education and culture.

objectives: Compare it with the California Constitution

days.title: U.S. Constitution
days.work: Read the Preamble and identify the six goals of the U.S. government.

days.title: Three branches
days.work: Make a chart of the legislative, executive and judicial branches.

days.title: California Constitution
days.work: Read the California Constitution's preamble and Declaration of Rights excerpts.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Complete a Venn diagram comparing federal and state governments.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz on the U.S. and California constitutions and the three branches of government.

objectives: Explain the structures and functions of state government

days.title: Executive
days.work: Read about the governor and other elected officials (lieutenant governor, attorney general).

days.title: Legislature
days.work: Read about the Assembly and Senate and how a bill becomes law.

days.title: Your legislators
days.work: Look up your state Assembly member and senator and their committee roles.

days.title: Courts
days.work: Read about the California Supreme Court and state courts and explain the job of the judicial branch.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a letter to your state legislator about an issue that matters to you.

days.title: Local governments
days.work: Identify your city, county, school district and nearest rancheria or reservation.

days.title: City council
days.work: Watch part of a city council meeting online and list topics discussed.

days.title: Tribal government
days.work: Read about a California tribal government and its services.

days.title: Year timeline
days.work: Build a California history timeline from first peoples to today.

days.title: Final assessment
days.work: Take the end-of-year HSS assessment covering geography, first peoples, missions, Gold Rush, statehood and government.

courses.subject: VAPA
courses.title: Art & Music 4
courses.description: Grade 4 visual art and music aligned to the 2019 California Arts Standards. Units alternate between visual art (drawing, color and landscape, cultural art forms of California, sculpture and printmaking) and music (rhythm and meter, beginning soprano recorder, melody and notation, composition, musical traditions of California). The year ends with a curated art exhibition and a recorder concert for family.
courses.framework: 2019 California Arts Standards for Public Schools, Prekindergarten Through Grade Twelve (Visual Arts and Music); 2020 CA Arts Framework

standards.VA:Cr1.1.4: Brainstorm multiple approaches to a creative art or design problem.
standards.VA:Cr1.2.4: Collaboratively set goals and create artwork that is meaningful and has purpose to the makers.
standards.VA:Cr2.1.4: Explore and invent art-making techniques and approaches.
standards.VA:Cr2.2.4: When making works of art, utilize and care for materials, tools and equipment in a manner that prevents danger to oneself and others.
standards.VA:Cr2.3.4: Document, describe and represent regional constructed environments.
standards.VA:Cr3.1.4: Revise artwork in progress on the basis of insights gained through peer discussion.
standards.VA:Pr4.1.4: Analyze how past, present and emerging technologies have impacted the preservation and presentation of artwork.
standards.VA:Pr5.1.4: Analyze the various considerations for presenting and protecting art in various locations, indoor or outdoor settings, in temporary or permanent forms.
standards.VA:Pr6.1.4: Compare and contrast purposes of art museums, art galleries and other venues, as well as the types of personal experiences they provide.
standards.VA:Re7.1.4: Compare responses to a work of art before and after working in similar media.
standards.VA:Re7.2.4: Analyze components in visual imagery that convey messages.
standards.VA:Re8.1.4: Interpret art by referring to contextual information and analyzing relevant subject matter, characteristics of form and use of media.
standards.VA:Re9.1.4: Apply one set of criteria to evaluate more than one work of art.
standards.VA:Cn10.1.4: Create works of art that reflect community cultural traditions.
standards.VA:Cn11.1.4: Through observation, infer information about time, place and culture in which a work of art was created.
standards.MU:Cr1.1.4: Improvise rhythmic, melodic and harmonic ideas, and explain connection to specific purpose and context.
standards.MU:Cr2.1.4: Demonstrate selected and organized musical ideas for an improvisation, arrangement or composition to express intent; use standard and/or iconic notation to document them.
standards.MU:Cr3.1.4: Evaluate, refine and document revisions to personal music, applying teacher-provided and collaboratively developed criteria and feedback.
standards.MU:Cr3.2.4: Present the final version of personal created music to others, and explain connection to expressive intent.
standards.MU:Pr4.1.4: Demonstrate and explain how the selection of music to perform is influenced by personal interest, knowledge, context and technical skill.
standards.MU:Pr4.2.4: Demonstrate understanding of the structure and the elements of music (rhythm, pitch and form) in music selected for performance; read and perform using iconic and standard notation.
standards.MU:Pr4.3.4: Demonstrate and explain how intent is conveyed through interpretive decisions and expressive qualities (dynamics, tempo, timbre, articulation/style).
standards.MU:Pr5.1.4: Apply teacher-provided and collaboratively developed criteria and feedback to evaluate accuracy and expressiveness of ensemble and personal performances; rehearse to refine.
standards.MU:Pr6.1.4: Perform music, alone or with others, with expression, technical accuracy and appropriate interpretation; demonstrate performance decorum and audience etiquette.
standards.MU:Re7.1.4: Demonstrate and explain how selected music connects to and is influenced by specific interests, experiences, purposes or contexts.
standards.MU:Re7.2.4: Demonstrate and explain how responses to music are informed by the structure, the use of the elements of music and context (social and cultural).
standards.MU:Re8.1.4: Demonstrate and explain how the expressive qualities (dynamics, tempo, timbre, articulation) are used in performers' and personal interpretations to reflect expressive intent.
standards.MU:Re9.1.4: Evaluate musical works and performances, applying established criteria, and explain appropriateness to the context.
standards.MU:Cn10.0.4: Demonstrate how interests, knowledge and skills relate to personal choices and intent when creating, performing and responding to music.
standards.MU:Cn11.0.4: Demonstrate understanding of relationships between music and the other arts, other disciplines, varied contexts and daily life.

units.title: Drawing: Line, Shape and Value
units.big_idea: Artists use line, shape and value to show what they observe and imagine.

units.title: Rhythm, Meter and Beginning Recorder
units.big_idea: Music is organized by steady beat, rhythm and meter, and the recorder lets us play melodies.

units.title: Color and the California Landscape
units.big_idea: Artists use color, space and media to express feelings about places.

units.title: Melody, Notation and California Folk Songs
units.big_idea: Melodies move by step and skip, and songs carry the stories of their time and place.

units.title: Art and Culture in California
units.big_idea: Art from many cultures in California reflects traditions, beliefs and community.

units.title: Composing Music and Musical Form
units.big_idea: Composers organize musical ideas into forms like AB, ABA and rondo.

units.title: Sculpture, Printmaking and Built Environments
units.big_idea: Three-dimensional art and prints transform materials, and architecture shapes how communities look.

units.title: Musical Traditions of California and the World
units.big_idea: Music connects to the cultures, purposes and experiences of the people who make it.

units.title: Exhibition and Concert
units.big_idea: Artists and musicians select, refine and present their best work to an audience.

objectives: Use varied lines to describe objects
Practice contour and blind contour drawing

days.title: Sketchbook start
days.work: Decorate a sketchbook cover and fill one page with 15 kinds of lines (zigzag, broken, thick-thin, spiral).

days.title: Blind contour
days.work: Draw your own hand three times without looking at the paper, then once looking; compare the results.

days.title: Contour still life
days.work: Draw a contour line drawing of three kitchen objects (mug, spoon, fruit) arranged on a table.

days.title: Line in art
days.work: Look at a Van Gogh reed-pen drawing online and list the lines he used for grass, sky and trees.

days.title: Review & share
days.work: Choose the best contour drawing, add a title and explain your line choices to a family member.

weeks.topic: Shape and form: shading with value
objectives: Turn shapes into forms with value

days.title: Value scale
days.work: Create a 7-step value scale from white to black with a 4B pencil.

days.title: Light and shadow
days.work: Shine a flashlight on a ball and identify highlight, midtone, core shadow and cast shadow.

days.title: Shade a sphere
days.work: Draw and shade a sphere, cube and cylinder using the value scale.

days.title: Hatching
days.work: Practice hatching, cross-hatching and stippling in a 3-box chart.

days.title: Review & share
days.work: Shade a piece of fruit from observation and compare it with the week 1 contour drawing.

days.title: Nature walk
days.work: Collect 5 natural objects (leaves, pinecone, feather) on a walk.

days.title: Viewfinder
days.work: Make a cardstock viewfinder and sketch 4 small compositions of the objects.

days.title: Detailed study
days.work: Draw one object large, filling the page, with contour and value.

days.title: Artist look
days.work: Look at John James Audubon bird drawings and compare your response before and after your own nature study.

days.title: Review & share
days.work: Write 3 sentences on what you noticed by drawing that you didn't notice by looking.

days.title: Criteria
days.work: Make a 4-point checklist for a strong drawing (fills page, line variety, value range, detail).

days.title: Critique
days.work: Discuss two of your drawings with a parent using 'I notice / I wonder / I suggest'.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise one drawing based on feedback, adding value or detail.

days.title: Final drawing
days.work: Create a finished observational drawing of a household object using all skills.

days.title: Review & share
days.work: Self-assess the final drawing with the checklist and display it.

days.title: Beat vs rhythm
days.work: Pat the steady beat while saying the rhythm of 'Old MacDonald' and explain the difference.

days.title: Rhythm notation
days.work: Read and clap quarter notes, eighth notes, half notes and rests from 8 rhythm cards.

days.title: Meter
days.work: Conduct 2/4, 3/4 and 4/4 patterns to recordings of a march and a waltz.

days.title: Improvise
days.work: Improvise 4-beat rhythms on a bucket drum in a call-and-response with a parent.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Clap 4 rhythm patterns and identify the meter of 3 songs.

objectives: Hold and play the recorder with good tone

days.title: Recorder care
days.work: Learn posture, left-hand-on-top hold and gentle 'doo' tonguing; play B.

days.title: B and A
days.work: Play B and A in quarter and half notes from notation.

days.title: Add G
days.work: Add G and play 'Hot Cross Buns' from the staff.

days.title: Note reading
days.work: Write letter names for B, A, G on a staff worksheet.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Play 'Hot Cross Buns' and 'Gently Sleep' for a parent.

weeks.topic: Recorder songs with B-A-G and C, D
objectives: Play songs with B, A, G, high C and D

days.title: High C and D
days.work: Learn high C and D fingerings and play scales B-C-D.

days.title: Mary Had a Little Lamb
days.work: Play 'Mary Had a Little Lamb' using B, A and G from notation, keeping a steady beat.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse 'Merrily We Roll Along' and 'Ode to Joy' excerpt.

days.title: Record and evaluate
days.work: Record your playing and evaluate tone and rhythm accuracy.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Play 'Mary Had a Little Lamb' and 'Merrily We Roll Along' for a parent, who checks tone and steady beat.

objectives: Perform rhythm and recorder parts together

days.title: Ostinato
days.work: Create a 4-beat rhythm ostinato to accompany a recorder song.

days.title: Layering
days.work: Play the recorder melody while a family member plays the ostinato.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse the melody and ostinato together with a metronome at 80 beats per minute.

days.title: Etiquette
days.work: Practice performer and audience etiquette (bow, quiet listening, applause).

days.title: Mini-concert
days.work: Perform for family and evaluate with a 3-point rubric.

objectives: Mix primary, secondary and tertiary colors

days.title: Color wheel
days.work: Paint a 12-part color wheel mixing only red, yellow and blue.

days.title: Tints and shades
days.work: Make tint and shade strips by adding white and black to one color.

days.title: Warm vs cool
days.work: Paint two small abstract designs, one warm and one cool, and compare moods.

days.title: Complements
days.work: Paint complementary color pairs side by side and observe contrast.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on color vocabulary using the color wheel.

weeks.topic: Landscape space: foreground, middle ground, background

days.title: Depth tricks
days.work: Look at a California landscape painting by a California Impressionist (e.g., Guy Rose) and find foreground, middle and background.

days.title: Atmospheric perspective
days.work: Draw three mountain ranges getting lighter as they recede.

days.title: Sketch
days.work: Sketch a California landscape (Yosemite, coast or desert) with overlapping layers.

days.title: Color
days.work: Add warm colors in front and cool colors behind.

days.title: Review & share
days.work: Explain to family how overlap, size, placement and color show depth in your landscape.

weeks.topic: Watercolor landscape and Ansel Adams photography
objectives: Compare painting and photography of landscapes

days.title: Techniques
days.work: Practice flat wash, gradated wash and wet-on-wet skies.

days.title: Paint
days.work: Paint the week 10 landscape in watercolor, painting the sky first and the foreground last.

days.title: Ansel Adams
days.work: Study Ansel Adams' 'Monolith, the Face of Half Dome' and discuss value and contrast.

days.title: Photograph
days.work: Take 5 black-and-white photos of your neighborhood using Adams' ideas of contrast.

days.title: Review & share
days.work: Compare your painting and photos in a short written response.

objectives: Apply criteria to evaluate multiple artworks

days.title: Criteria
days.work: Develop criteria for a successful landscape (depth, color, mood, technique).

days.title: Evaluate masters
days.work: Apply the criteria to 3 landscapes by different artists (Bierstadt, Hokusai, a California Impressionist).

days.title: Self-evaluate
days.work: Apply the same criteria to your own landscape.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Add finishing details to improve one criterion.

days.title: Review & share
days.work: Present the landscape and evaluation to family.

objectives: Add low E and D to the recorder

days.title: Melodic contour
days.work: Listen to 3 melodies ('Twinkle', 'Ode to Joy', 'Somewhere Over the Rainbow') and draw each melody's up-and-down shape.

days.title: Low E and D
days.work: Learn low E and D fingerings, covering holes fully, and play long tones on each.

days.title: Steps and skips
days.work: Circle steps, skips and leaps in the written melody of 'Ode to Joy' and then play it.

days.title: Note naming
days.work: Name 20 notes from low D to high D on a treble staff worksheet.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Play a D-to-D scale up and down and sight-read a 4-measure stepwise melody.

objectives: Sing and play California folk songs
materials: lyrics of 'Oh My Darling, Clementine' and 'Sweet Betsy from Pike'

days.title: Clementine
days.work: Sing 'Oh My Darling, Clementine' and discuss what the lyrics tell about a forty-niner's family.

days.title: Sweet Betsy
days.work: Sing 'Sweet Betsy from Pike' and trace Betsy and Ike's overland journey on a map.

days.title: Play Clementine
days.work: Learn the 'Clementine' melody on recorder in G, two phrases at a time.

days.title: Context writing
days.work: Write 3 sentences on what these ballads reveal about Gold Rush life and why people sang them.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform one Gold Rush song (sung or played) and explain why you chose it.

objectives: Use dynamics and tempo to convey intent
materials: recording of Grieg's 'In the Hall of the Mountain King'

days.title: Dynamics
days.work: Play 'Clementine' piano and then forte, and add a crescendo to one phrase.

days.title: Tempo
days.work: Play 'Ode to Joy' at largo, moderato and allegro tempos with a metronome app.

days.title: Listening map
days.work: Listen to 'In the Hall of the Mountain King' and draw a listening map of its growing tempo and dynamics.

days.title: Interpretation plan
days.work: Mark dynamics and tempo on a folk song's music to match the story's mood.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform the folk song with your planned expression and explain each choice.

objectives: Select, rehearse and perform melodies from notation

days.title: Choose repertoire
days.work: Choose two recorder pieces learned this unit and explain why they fit your skill level and interests.

days.title: Section rehearsal
days.work: Rehearse the hardest 4 measures of each piece slowly, then at tempo.

days.title: Record
days.work: Record a full run-through of both pieces without stopping.

days.title: Evaluate
days.work: Listen back and score tone, rhythm, notes and expression with a 4-point rubric; fix two problems.

days.title: Perform
days.work: Perform both pieces for family with a spoken introduction for each.

materials: Calisphere set 'Native Americans: Arts and Traditions'

days.title: Look closely
days.work: Study Pomo and Chumash basket images on Calisphere and describe shapes, patterns and materials.

days.title: Infer
days.work: Write what the baskets suggest about the makers' environment, skills and daily life.

days.title: Weaving loom
days.work: Make a paper-plate loom and begin weaving a yarn pattern.

days.title: Pattern design
days.work: Design a repeating geometric motif inspired by (not copied from) the baskets and finish the weaving.

days.title: Review & share
days.work: Explain your pattern choices and what you learned about basketry as a living tradition.

weeks.topic: Papel picado and Mexican folk art
objectives: Create a cut-paper design reflecting a community tradition
materials: images of papel picado and alebrijes

days.title: Folk art tour
days.work: Look at images of papel picado, alebrijes and Talavera pottery and discuss when and why they are made.

days.title: Positive/negative space
days.work: Practice folding and cutting symmetrical shapes and identify positive and negative space.

days.title: Design
days.work: Sketch a papel picado design with a theme (celebration, nature, family).

days.title: Cut
days.work: Cut 3 tissue paper banners and string them together.

days.title: Review & share
days.work: Hang the banner and explain its symbols and the tradition it comes from.

objectives: Use brush techniques from Chinese painting
Connect art to Chinese American heritage in California

days.title: Look
days.work: Study a classical Chinese bamboo painting and discuss balance and empty space.

days.title: Strokes
days.work: Practice the four basic strokes: bamboo stalk, leaf, dot and line.

days.title: Bamboo painting
days.work: Paint a bamboo stalk with leaves using ink washes of different values.

days.title: Context
days.work: Read about Chinese American artists in California (e.g., Tyrus Wong) and their influence.

days.title: Review & share
days.work: Finish a painting with a seal-style signature and compare it to your earlier work.

objectives: Collaboratively plan an artwork with purpose
materials: photos of murals (e.g., Chicano Park, Balmy Alley)

days.title: Mural study
days.work: Look at photos of murals in Chicano Park (San Diego) or Balmy Alley (San Francisco) and discuss their messages.

days.title: Set goals
days.work: With family members, choose a theme about your community and set goals for the mural.

days.title: Sketch
days.work: Each person sketches ideas; combine the best into one plan.

days.title: Paint/draw
days.work: Create the mural on a large sheet of paper together.

days.title: Review & share
days.work: Write an artist statement explaining the mural's message and display it.

weeks.topic: Musical form: AB, ABA and rondo
objectives: Show form with movement and symbols

days.title: AB form
days.work: Listen to a two-part song and hold up shapes when the A and B sections change.

days.title: ABA form
days.work: Listen to 'Twinkle, Twinkle' as ABA and label the sections in the lyrics.

days.title: Rondo
days.work: Listen to Mozart's 'Rondo alla Turca' and track the ABACA form.

days.title: Movement
days.work: Create a different movement for each section of a rondo and perform it.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Listen to 3 new pieces and identify each form (AB, ABA or rondo) with a labeled diagram.

objectives: Compose short melodies with standard notation

days.title: Improvise
days.work: Improvise 4-beat answers on recorder using B, A and G to a parent's 4-beat questions.

days.title: Motive
days.work: Create a 2-measure melodic motive and repeat it with changes.

days.title: Song Maker
days.work: Compose an 8-measure melody in Chrome Music Lab Song Maker.

days.title: Notate
days.work: Notate the melody on staff paper with rhythm and pitch.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Play the 8-measure composition on recorder and record it for next week's revision.

days.title: Plan contrast
days.work: Plan an ABA piece: what will make B different (tempo, dynamics, pitch range)?

days.title: Write B
days.work: Compose an 8-measure B section that contrasts with the A section from week 22.

days.title: Feedback
days.work: Play the draft for a parent and gather feedback with a 3-question form.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise two measures based on feedback and record the changes.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a short description of the piece's form and mood.

days.title: Program note
days.work: Write a program note explaining your composition's title and intent.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse the ABA piece with dynamics and tempo markings.

days.title: Premiere
days.work: Perform the premiere of your composition for family.

days.title: Evaluate
days.work: Watch two recorded youth performances online and evaluate them with criteria.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Self-evaluate your premiere using the same criteria.

objectives: Create a sculpture using pinch and coil methods

days.title: Clay basics
days.work: Learn safe clay handling and make a pinch pot.

days.title: Coils
days.work: Roll coils and add them to build a taller vessel or animal.

days.title: Texture
days.work: Press found objects into clay to create textures.

days.title: Sculpt
days.work: Sculpt a California animal (sea otter, quail, bear) using score-and-slip joins.

days.title: Review & share
days.work: Let dry and describe your process and safety steps.

materials: foam meat trays or styrofoam sheets

days.title: Printmaking history
days.work: Look at Japanese woodblock prints and discuss repetition.

days.title: Design
days.work: Brainstorm 3 designs and choose one; remember it will print in reverse.

days.title: Carve plate
days.work: Incise the design into a foam plate with a dull pencil.

days.title: Print
days.work: Roll paint and pull an edition of 4 prints in different colors.

days.title: Review & share
days.work: Sign and number the edition and choose the best print.

objectives: Document and represent regional built environments

days.title: Styles
days.work: Compare images of a mission adobe, a San Francisco Victorian, a Craftsman bungalow and a mid-century modern house.

days.title: Neighborhood walk
days.work: Photograph and sketch 4 buildings in your neighborhood.

days.title: Details
days.work: Draw close-up details (windows, roofs, doors) of one building.

days.title: Design a building
days.work: Design a building for your community and draw its facade.

days.title: Review & share
days.work: Explain how your design fits California's climate and community.

days.title: Feedback
days.work: Get feedback on sculpture and prints using 'I notice / I wonder / I suggest'.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Paint the dried clay sculpture with acrylic or tempera and add details suggested in feedback.

days.title: Display plan
days.work: Plan where to display the sculpture safely (stable surface, away from edges and sunlight) and sketch the setup.

days.title: Labels
days.work: Write gallery labels for the sculpture and best print with title, medium, date and a one-sentence description.

days.title: Review & share
days.work: Install the sculpture and prints and give a 2-minute talk to family about your process.

weeks.topic: Mariachi and Mexican music in California
objectives: Explain how music connects to culture

days.title: Listen
days.work: Listen to 'El Son de la Negra' and identify instruments: violin, trumpet, vihuela, guitarrón.

days.title: Timbre
days.work: Describe the timbre of each instrument with adjectives.

days.title: Context
days.work: Read about mariachi at celebrations in California communities.

days.title: Rhythm
days.work: Clap the 3/4 + 6/8 alternating rhythm (sesquialtera).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write how mariachi connects to family celebrations.

weeks.topic: Taiko, gamelan and Asian American music

days.title: Taiko
days.work: Watch San Jose Taiko and describe movement and sound.

days.title: Bucket taiko
days.work: Learn a 4-beat taiko pattern on a bucket with kiai shouts.

days.title: Gamelan
days.work: Listen to Balinese gamelan and identify layered patterns.

days.title: Compose
days.work: Create a layered rhythm piece with 3 repeating parts on bucket, pot and shaker and notate it.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform the taiko piece and compare taiko and gamelan.

objectives: Identify features of jazz and blues
materials: recordings (Dave Brubeck 'Take Five', Ella Fitzgerald scat)

days.title: Blues form
days.work: Listen to a 12-bar blues (e.g., 'C-Jam Blues') and clap on the first beat of each of the 12 bars.

days.title: Swing
days.work: Practice swung eighth notes ('doo-ba doo-ba') on recorder on B, A and G.

days.title: Improvise
days.work: Improvise with B, A, G over a blues backing track.

days.title: California jazz
days.work: Listen to Dave Brubeck's 'Take Five' and identify the 5/4 meter.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Evaluate a jazz recording using criteria (steady groove, creative improvisation, expression) and write a short review.

objectives: Connect music to other arts and daily life

days.title: Film music
days.work: Watch a film clip with and without sound and describe the mood change.

days.title: Kandinsky
days.work: Draw in Chrome Music Lab's Kandinsky to turn art into sound.

days.title: Soundtrack
days.work: Create a soundtrack for a short story using recorder and percussion.

days.title: Personal playlist
days.work: Make a playlist of 5 songs that represent you and explain choices.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Unit test on musical traditions and connections.

objectives: Select artwork for an exhibition using criteria
Analyze how technology preserves and presents art

days.title: Review the year
days.work: Lay out every artwork from the year, sort by unit, and note which skills each shows.

days.title: Select
days.work: Select 6 pieces for an exhibition using one set of criteria (skill, idea, growth) and record a score for each.

days.title: Digital portfolio
days.work: Photograph each piece in good light and create a digital portfolio slideshow with titles.

days.title: Preservation
days.work: Read how museums such as the Getty protect artworks (light, humidity, digital archives) and list 3 ways technology helps preserve art.

days.title: Curator's statement
days.work: Write a one-paragraph curator's statement explaining the exhibition's theme and choices.

weeks.assessment: Curated selection, digital portfolio and statement.

objectives: Plan how to present and protect art in a chosen space
Compare the purposes of museums, galleries and other venues

days.title: Venues compared
days.work: Compare an art museum, a commercial gallery and a community art walk in a chart: purpose, who visits, what experience they give.

days.title: Mat and label
days.work: Mount the 6 artworks on cardstock mats and write museum-style labels (title, artist, medium, year, one-sentence description).

days.title: Protecting art
days.work: Decide how to protect each piece where it will hang (away from sunlight, sculpture on a stable shelf) and explain why.

days.title: Layout and install
days.work: Sketch a floor plan of the exhibit wall, then hang the work at eye level with even spacing.

days.title: Walkthrough
days.work: Lead a family member on a guided tour and revise any label that was unclear.

objectives: Select concert repertoire based on interest, context and skill

days.title: Choose program
days.work: Choose 4 pieces (a folk song, a classical excerpt, your ABA composition and a free choice) and explain why each belongs.

days.title: Targeted practice
days.work: Practice the two hardest passages slowly with a metronome, raising the tempo 10 beats at a time.

days.title: Feedback round
days.work: Record a run-through, get feedback from a family member, and mark dynamics changes on the music.

days.title: Design program
days.work: Design a printed concert program with piece titles, composers and short program notes.

days.title: Dress rehearsal
days.work: Hold a full dress rehearsal including bows and spoken introductions, and fix one remaining problem.

objectives: Perform with expression and accuracy for an audience
Reflect on artistic growth across the year

days.title: Warm-up routine
days.work: Lead your own 10-minute warm-up: long tones, a D-to-D scale and the toughest phrase from each piece.

days.title: Exhibition opening
days.work: Host the exhibition opening, giving guests a 3-minute tour and answering questions about techniques.

days.title: Concert
days.work: Perform the 4-piece recorder concert with introductions and proper stage etiquette.

days.title: Reflection
days.work: Write a one-page reflection comparing week 1 drawings and recorder playing to now, using the year's vocabulary.

days.title: Goal setting
days.work: Watch the concert recording, evaluate it with the class rubric, and set two art and music goals for grade 5.

weeks.assessment: Concert and exhibition evaluated with rubric; written reflection.

courses.subject: PE
courses.title: PE 4
courses.description: Grade 4 physical education aligned to the California Physical Education Model Content Standards and Framework. Students refine manipulative skills (overhand throwing, catching, foot dribbling, hand dribbling, striking and volleying), perform long-rope jumping, balance stunts and folk dances, and apply movement concepts and simple strategies in small-sided games. Fitness is assessed with FITNESSGRAM-style tests at the start and end of the year, and students set personal goals, track heart rate and practice cooperation and sportsmanship.
courses.framework: California Physical Education Model Content Standards (Grade 4); 2009 California Physical Education Framework

standards.PE-4.1.1: Perform simple small-group balance stunts by distributing weight and base of support.
standards.PE-4.1.2: Perform intermediate-level, long-rope jumping skills (e.g., entering and exiting a turning rope, double turns).
standards.PE-4.1.3: Perform locomotor and nonlocomotor movements in rhythmic patterns and folk/line dances.
standards.PE-4.1.4: Throw a ball overhand with accuracy to a target and for distance using mature form.
standards.PE-4.1.5: Catch a thrown or kicked ball above the waist, below the waist and while moving.
standards.PE-4.1.6: Dribble and pass a ball with the feet (inside and outside of the foot) while moving and changing direction.
standards.PE-4.1.7: Dribble a ball with the hands while moving, changing speed and direction, and pass to a moving partner.
standards.PE-4.1.8: Strike an object with a paddle, racket or bat using a sideways orientation and controlled force.
standards.PE-4.1.9: Volley an object upward and to a partner using hands and forearms.
standards.PE-4.2.1: Explain how to use body position, force and follow-through to improve throwing, kicking and striking.
standards.PE-4.2.2: Explain how to create and reduce space when moving with others in game situations (offense and defense).
standards.PE-4.2.3: Design and refine a movement sequence or dance using changes in level, pathway, tempo and force.
standards.PE-4.3.1: Participate in moderate-to-vigorous physical activity for increasing periods of time (aerobic capacity).
standards.PE-4.3.2: Perform exercises that build muscular strength and endurance (curl-ups, push-ups).
standards.PE-4.3.3: Perform exercises that improve flexibility (trunk lift, sit-and-reach).
standards.PE-4.3.4: Assess personal fitness with standardized tests and set short-term fitness goals.
standards.PE-4.3.5: Monitor heart rate before, during and after physical activity.
standards.PE-4.4.1: Explain the relationship between heart rate, breathing and intensity of physical activity.
standards.PE-4.4.2: Identify the five components of health-related fitness and activities that develop each.
standards.PE-4.4.3: Explain the importance of warm-up, cool-down, hydration and safety in physical activity.
standards.PE-4.5.1: Demonstrate sportsmanship and respect for others during activities, winning or losing.
standards.PE-4.5.2: Work cooperatively with a partner or small group to solve movement problems and accomplish goals.
standards.PE-4.5.3: Use conflict-resolution strategies (e.g., rock-paper-scissors, talk it out, take turns) during games.
