units.title: Fitness Foundations and Pre-Assessment
units.big_idea: Knowing our starting fitness lets us set goals and track growth.

units.title: Throwing and Catching
units.big_idea: Stepping with the opposite foot, rotating and following through produce accurate, powerful throws.

units.title: Foot Skills: Dribble, Pass and Trap
units.big_idea: Soft touches and open space help a team keep and move the ball.

units.title: Jump Rope and Rhythm
units.big_idea: Timing and rhythm let us jump individually and with long ropes for fun fitness.

units.title: Balance, Tumbling and Stunts
units.big_idea: A wide, low base of support makes balances stable, alone and in groups.

units.title: Hand Dribbling and Passing
units.big_idea: Dribbling with fingerpads and eyes up lets us move and pass to open teammates.

units.title: Folk and Line Dance
units.big_idea: Dance builds rhythm and connects us to the cultures of California.

units.title: Striking and Volleying
units.big_idea: A side-facing stance, level swing and firm contact control where the object goes.

units.title: Cooperative and Strategy Games
units.big_idea: Teams win by communicating, creating space and playing fair.

units.title: Fitness Post-Assessment and Field Day
units.big_idea: Comparing results shows growth and helps plan lifelong activity.

objectives: Perform a dynamic warm-up and cool-down
Measure resting and active heart rate

days.title: Dynamic warm-up
days.work: Learn a 5-minute warm-up (high knees, butt kicks, arm circles, lunges, inchworms) and lead it once.

days.title: Find your pulse
days.work: Count your pulse for 15 seconds at rest, multiply by 4, and log it; repeat after 2 minutes of jumping jacks.

days.title: Heart rate zones
days.work: Do 3 activities of different intensity (walk, jog, sprint) and record heart rate after each.

days.title: Cool-down & hydration
days.work: Learn 4 static stretches for the cool-down and track water intake for the day.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain to a parent why heart rate rises with intensity and lead the full warm-up and cool-down.

weeks.assessment: Heart rate log and led warm-up.

days.title: Five components
days.work: Match 10 activities to the five health-related fitness components.

days.title: PACER or mile
days.work: Complete the 20-meter PACER (or a timed 1-mile walk/run) and record laps or time.

days.title: Curl-ups & push-ups
days.work: Complete cadence curl-ups and 90-degree push-ups tests and record results.

days.title: Trunk lift & sit-and-reach
days.work: Complete trunk lift and back-saver sit-and-reach tests and record results.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Compare results to Healthy Fitness Zone charts with a parent.

days.title: SMART goals
days.work: Write two SMART fitness goals based on pre-assessment results.

days.title: Circuit design
days.work: Set up a 6-station circuit (jumping jacks, plank, wall sit, jump rope, step-ups, crab walk) for 40 seconds each.

days.title: Circuit day
days.work: Complete the circuit twice with 20-second rests and log repetitions.

days.title: Family challenge
days.work: Teach a family member the circuit and complete it together.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Repeat the circuit and compare repetitions to day 3.

days.title: Cues
days.work: Learn the cues: side to target, arm back, step with opposite foot, rotate hips, follow through.

days.title: Wall throws
days.work: Throw 30 balls at a taped wall target from 15 feet, focusing on stepping.

days.title: Video check
days.work: Record your throw in slow motion and check each cue.

days.title: Distance throws
days.work: Throw for distance 10 times and measure the best three.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Demonstrate a throw while a parent scores the 5 cues.

objectives: Catch above and below the waist

days.title: Hand position
days.work: Practice thumbs-together catches high and pinkies-together catches low (30 tosses).

days.title: Partner catch
days.work: Play partner catch, stepping back after every 3 successful catches.

days.title: Moving catch
days.work: Run a pattern and catch a ball tossed ahead of you.

days.title: Bounce catch
days.work: Play a reaction-bounce game with a playground ball.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a 20-catch test at three levels and record the score.

days.title: Lead passes
days.work: Throw to a partner jogging across the yard, aiming ahead of them.

days.title: Disc throw
days.work: Learn the backhand flying-disc throw and complete 20 partner throws.

days.title: Football spiral
days.work: Practice gripping and throwing a junior football in a spiral.

days.title: Target game
days.work: Play a 'hit the cone' accuracy game from three distances.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Score accuracy on 10 throws to a moving partner.

days.title: Ultimate disc basics
days.work: Learn ultimate disc rules (no running with the disc, pivot foot) and play a 2-on-2 game.

days.title: Sportsmanship talk
days.work: List 5 sportsmanship behaviors and practice them in a game.

days.title: Hot potato relay
days.work: Play a timed throwing and catching relay with family.

days.title: Skill review
days.work: Review throwing and catching cues by teaching them to a sibling or parent.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Complete a throwing and catching skills test and a sportsmanship self-rating.

objectives: Dribble with inside and outside of the foot

days.title: Touches
days.work: Practice toe taps, inside-inside touches and sole rolls for 5 minutes.

days.title: Cone weave
days.work: Dribble through 6 cones using inside and outside of the foot.

days.title: Speed changes
days.work: Dribble at walking, jogging and running speed on a whistle.

days.title: Red light, green light
days.work: Play dribbling red light, green light, stopping the ball with the sole.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Time a cone-weave dribble 3 times and record the best.

objectives: Pass with the inside of the foot

days.title: Inside-foot pass
days.work: Pass to a wall 30 times with each foot, plant foot beside the ball.

days.title: Trapping
days.work: Trap balls rolled at different speeds with sole and inside of foot.

days.title: Partner passing
days.work: Pass back and forth with a partner, increasing distance.

days.title: Gate passing
days.work: Pass through cone gates scattered across the yard.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Count successful passes through a gate in 2 minutes.

days.title: Open space
days.work: Play keep-away 2-on-1, moving to open space to receive.

days.title: Defense
days.work: Practice defensive stance and staying goal-side.

days.title: Small-sided game
days.work: Play a 2-on-2 soccer game with small cone goals, calling for the ball when open.

days.title: Strategy talk
days.work: Draw a diagram showing how to create space on offense.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Self-assess moving to space using a 3-point checklist.

days.title: Skills stations
days.work: Rotate through dribbling, passing and shooting stations.

days.title: Conflict resolution
days.work: Practice resolving a disputed call with rock-paper-scissors.

days.title: Game day
days.work: Play a family soccer game with kick-ins, no hands and fair-play rules for 15 minutes.

days.title: Refereeing
days.work: Referee a short game, making calls for out-of-bounds and handballs and explaining each.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Complete a foot skills test: cone-weave dribble, 10 gate passes and 5 traps scored by a parent.

objectives: Perform basic and intermediate short-rope jumps

days.title: Rope sizing & basic bounce
days.work: Size the rope (handles reach armpits when standing on its center) and practice the basic two-foot bounce for 4 sets of 30 seconds.

days.title: Skier and bell
days.work: Learn the skier (side-to-side) and bell (front-to-back) jumps and do 20 of each without missing.

days.title: Criss-cross
days.work: Practice the criss-cross by crossing arms at the waist on every third jump; count successful crosses.

days.title: Endurance intervals
days.work: Jump five 30-second intervals with 30-second rests, recording jumps per interval and heart rate.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform a 4-trick routine (bounce, skier, bell, criss-cross) for a parent who scores it.

objectives: Enter and exit a turning long rope
materials: a partner or a post to tie one end

days.title: Turning
days.work: Practice turning a long rope with a partner, making full circles that tap the ground on each beat.

days.title: Front door
days.work: Enter the 'front door' as the rope comes toward you, jump 5 times and run out the far side.

days.title: Back door
days.work: Enter through the 'back door' (rope moving away) by waiting for it to hit the ground and following it in.

days.title: Chants
days.work: Jump to traditional rope chants like 'Teddy Bear, Teddy Bear' while doing the actions.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform a front-door entry, 10 jumps with a turn-around, and a clean exit.

objectives: Try Double Dutch turning and entry
Jump with a partner in one rope

days.title: Partner jumping
days.work: Jump side-by-side with a partner sharing one short rope, each turning one handle.

days.title: Double Dutch turning
days.work: Practice 'eggbeater' turning of two ropes in alternating circles with a family member and a post.

days.title: Double Dutch entry
days.work: Rock in time with the back rope, then enter and try 3 jumps; count best streak.

days.title: Routine design
days.work: With a partner, design a 4-part routine mixing partner jumps and single-rope tricks.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform the partner routine and give each other one compliment and one tip.

objectives: Use jump rope for aerobic fitness
Perform a rhythmic routine to music

days.title: Tabata jump
days.work: Do a 4-minute Tabata (20 seconds jumping, 10 seconds rest) and record heart rate after.

days.title: Choreograph
days.work: Choose a song and choreograph a 1-minute routine with at least 5 tricks matched to the beat.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse the routine 5 times, fixing any spot where you miss.

days.title: Perform
days.work: Perform the routine for family as a 'Jump Rope Show'.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Complete the jump rope skills test: 1-minute speed count, 3 tricks and long-rope entry.

objectives: Hold static balances with different bases of support
Explain why wide, low bases are stable

days.title: Bases of support
days.work: Hold 8 balances on different body parts (two hands and one foot, one knee and one hand) for 5 seconds each.

days.title: Stable or not?
days.work: Test narrow vs wide stances and explain which is more stable using 'center of gravity'.

days.title: Yoga balances
days.work: Practice tree, warrior III and boat pose, holding each for 15 seconds.

days.title: Safety
days.work: Learn safe falling (tuck and roll sideways) and spotting rules.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform 3 balances of your choice and explain the base of support for each.

objectives: Perform log roll, forward roll and cartwheel progressions safely

days.title: Rolls
days.work: Practice log rolls and egg rolls, then a forward roll down a gentle incline with chin tucked.

days.title: Cartwheel progression
days.work: Practice hand-hand-foot-foot along a line, then a lunge-to-cartwheel.

days.title: Flexibility
days.work: Do bridge, straddle stretch and butterfly stretch to improve tumbling flexibility.

days.title: Combine
days.work: Link a forward roll, stand, and balance into a smooth sequence.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform the forward roll and cartwheel for a parent who checks safety cues.

objectives: Perform small-group balances by distributing weight

days.title: Counterbalance
days.work: Practice partner sit-ups-to-stand back-to-back and lean-away holds with hands joined.

days.title: Partner stunts
days.work: Try partner balances such as the 'thigh stand' with a spotter, holding for 3 seconds.

days.title: Strength builders
days.work: Do planks, superman holds and wall sits to build the strength stunts need.

days.title: Group shape
days.work: With 2-3 family members, create a group balance that has at least 4 points of contact with the floor.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform 2 partner stunts and the group balance; discuss what communication made them work.

objectives: Design a movement sequence with balance, rolls and changes in level

days.title: Plan
days.work: Plan a routine with a start shape, 2 balances, 1 roll, 1 jump and a finish, using high, medium and low levels.

days.title: Transitions
days.work: Practice smooth transitions between each element.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse the routine 5 times, then record a final run-through on video.

days.title: Peer feedback
days.work: Watch the recording with a parent and revise one transition.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Perform the final routine; scored on control, levels, transitions and safety.

objectives: Dribble with fingerpads keeping eyes up
Dribble while changing speed and direction

days.title: Stationary
days.work: Practice pound dribbles, low dribbles and figure-8s around the legs with each hand.

days.title: Eyes up
days.work: Dribble while calling out the number of fingers a parent holds up.

days.title: Moving dribble
days.work: Dribble down and back on a line with right, left, then alternating hands.

days.title: Crossover
days.work: Learn the crossover dribble, switching hands low in front of the body around 6 cones.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a timed cone dribble course using both hands.

objectives: Use chest, bounce and overhead passes

days.title: Chest pass
days.work: Practice 30 chest passes to a wall target, stepping into each pass.

days.title: Bounce pass
days.work: Practice bounce passes that hit two-thirds of the way to the partner.

days.title: Overhead pass
days.work: Practice overhead passes and when to use them.

days.title: Moving passes
days.work: Pass to a partner jogging across the yard and catch with 'target hands'.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Score 10 chest, 10 bounce and 10 overhead passes to a partner's target hands.

materials: basketball and lowered hoop or laundry basket

days.title: BEEF shooting
days.work: Shoot 30 shots close to the hoop using BEEF cues.

days.title: Give-and-go
days.work: Practice give-and-go: pass to a partner, cut toward the basket and receive the return pass.

days.title: Defense
days.work: Practice defensive slide and keeping between the player and the basket.

days.title: 2-on-1
days.work: Play 2-on-1 with a passer, cutter and defender.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Record 5 shots on video and self-assess each BEEF cue on a checklist.

objectives: Apply dribbling, passing and shooting in games

days.title: Rules
days.work: Learn rules for traveling, double dribble and fouls and demonstrate each.

days.title: Half-court game
days.work: Play a 2-on-2 half-court basketball game to 7 points using the rules learned.

days.title: Conflict scenarios
days.work: Act out 3 disputed calls and resolve each with a fair strategy.

days.title: Skills stations
days.work: Rotate through dribble, pass and shoot stations.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Complete the hand dribble and passing skills test.

objectives: Perform steps of a Mexican folk dance

days.title: Watch & discuss
days.work: Watch a ballet folklórico performance video and describe the footwork and costumes.

days.title: La Raspa steps
days.work: Learn the La Raspa bleking step (alternating heels) in time with the music.

days.title: Partner figure
days.work: Learn the elbow-swing partner figure of La Raspa and connect it to the bleking section.

days.title: Full dance
days.work: Perform La Raspa from start to finish with a family member three times.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform for family and explain where the dance comes from.

objectives: Perform square dance calls and a line dance
Move with a partner and group
materials: square dance or Virginia reel music

days.title: Square dance calls
days.work: Learn do-si-do, swing your partner, promenade and allemande left.

days.title: Virginia reel
days.work: Dance the Virginia reel with family members, including the reel and the arch.

days.title: Grapevine
days.work: Learn the grapevine step and a 4-wall line dance (e.g., Cha Cha Slide).

days.title: Heart rate
days.work: Measure heart rate after dancing and compare to jogging.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform a sequence of called square dance moves without stopping.

objectives: Design a dance using level, pathway, tempo and force

days.title: Plan
days.work: Choose music and plan 4 eight-count sections using changes in level, pathway, tempo and force.

days.title: Teach
days.work: Teach your dance to a family member one eight-count at a time.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse the full dance with music and smooth out the transitions between sections.

days.title: Perform
days.work: Perform the dance for an audience and ask them to identify one level and one pathway change.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Self-assess the dance with a rubric and complete a dance steps check.

objectives: Strike a ball with a paddle using a side-facing stance

days.title: Grip & bumps
days.work: Learn the shake-hands grip and bump a ball upward 20 times.

days.title: Forehand
days.work: Practice forehand strikes against a wall from a sideways stance.

days.title: Backhand
days.work: Practice 30 backhand strikes against a wall, turning the shoulder toward the wall before each swing.

days.title: Rally
days.work: Rally with a partner over a low net (string between chairs).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Count your longest wall rally with forehand and backhand.

objectives: Strike a ball off a tee and from a toss

days.title: Stance & grip
days.work: Practice batting stance and grip with knuckles aligned.

days.title: Tee hitting
days.work: Hit 30 balls off a tee aiming for level swings.

days.title: Soft toss
days.work: Hit 20 soft-tossed balls from a parent, stepping toward the pitcher and swinging level.

days.title: Fielding
days.work: Practice fielding grounders and throwing to a base.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Play a game of whiffle ball with family and track hits.

objectives: Volley a ball upward with hands and forearms

days.title: Hand volley
days.work: Volley a beach ball upward with fingertips 20 times.

days.title: Forearm pass
days.work: Practice the bump with a platform of forearms.

days.title: Partner rally
days.work: Rally a beach ball with a partner using sets and bumps, counting hits.

days.title: Net game
days.work: Play a cooperative over-the-net game, counting consecutive hits.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Record your best cooperative rally of 3 tries and compare it to the start of the week.

days.title: Pickleball basics
days.work: Learn pickleball serve and scoring with family.

days.title: Mini-tournament
days.work: Play a family pickleball or paddle tournament.

days.title: Newcomb ball
days.work: Play Newcomb ball (catch-and-throw volleyball).

days.title: Sportsmanship
days.work: Write 3 sentences describing how you showed sportsmanship in the tournament.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Complete a striking and volleying skills test.

objectives: Solve movement problems with a group

days.title: Hula hoop pass
days.work: Pass a hula hoop around a circle of family members without letting go of hands; time three tries and improve.

days.title: Blindfold course
days.work: Guide a blindfolded partner through a cone course using words only, then switch roles.

days.title: Lava river
days.work: Cross a 10-foot 'lava river' as a group using only 3 paper-plate stepping stones.

days.title: Debrief
days.work: List the words and actions that helped the group succeed and one thing that caused frustration.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a cooperation self-rating (listening, encouraging, sharing ideas) and set one improvement goal.

objectives: Use dodging and faking to create space
Apply simple offensive and defensive strategies

days.title: Dodging
days.work: Practice dodging, faking and pivoting in a 'shadow' drill with a partner.

days.title: Flag tag
days.work: Play flag tag in a coned area, using fakes to keep your flags.

days.title: Capture the flag
days.work: Play capture the flag with family or neighbors, assigning defenders and attackers.

days.title: Strategy board
days.work: Draw a strategy diagram for your team and test it in a rematch.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write which strategy worked best and why, and how your team handled disagreements.

objectives: Invent a game that uses grade 4 skills
Write fair rules and teach them

days.title: Plan
days.work: Invent a game combining at least two skills (e.g., foot dribble and throwing) and list equipment and boundaries.

days.title: Rules
days.work: Write 5 rules, a scoring system and a safety rule on a poster.

days.title: Test
days.work: Play-test the game with family and note problems.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise rules to make the game fairer and more active.

days.title: Teach & play
days.work: Teach the final game to a new player and lead a full game.

days.title: Warm-up & PACER
days.work: Lead your dynamic warm-up and complete the PACER (or 1-mile run) and record the result.

days.title: Curl-ups & push-ups
days.work: Complete the cadence curl-up and 90-degree push-up tests and record results.

days.title: Trunk lift & sit-and-reach
days.work: Complete the trunk lift and sit-and-reach tests.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Graph pre- and post-test results side by side and check which goals you met.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph explaining what training helped most.

objectives: Explain how heart rate and fitness components connect

days.title: Fitness components quiz
days.work: Take a quiz on the five fitness components and heart rate concepts.

days.title: Favorite activities
days.work: List 10 activities you enjoy and which fitness component each builds.

days.title: Summer plan
days.work: Write a 4-week summer plan with 60 minutes of activity daily using frequency, intensity, time and type.

days.title: Try something new
days.work: Try a new activity (hiking trail, swimming, skating) and log heart rate.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present your plan to family and post it on the fridge.

objectives: Apply the year's skills in a field day

days.title: Plan field day
days.work: Plan 6 stations (sack race, accuracy throw, jump rope contest, dribble relay, tug-of-war, water relay) and make station signs.

days.title: Set up
days.work: Measure and set up stations safely and prepare a score card.

days.title: Field day
days.work: Run field day with family or friends, rotating through all stations.

days.title: Awards
days.work: Make sportsmanship awards for every participant.

days.title: Year reflection
days.work: Write a reflection on your favorite unit and the skill you improved most.

courses.subject: HEALTH
courses.title: Health 4
courses.description: Grade 4 health education aligned to the 2008 California Health Education Content Standards, which focus fourth grade on Nutrition and Physical Activity and on Alcohol, Tobacco and Other Drugs. Students learn nutrients and MyPlate, read Nutrition Facts labels, plan balanced meals and snacks, practice food safety, and set physical-activity goals; then they study safe medicine use, the effects of tobacco/vaping and alcohol, influences such as advertising and peers, and refusal and decision-making skills, finishing with a family health-promotion campaign.
courses.framework: 2008 California Health Education Content Standards (Grade 4: Nutrition and Physical Activity; Alcohol, Tobacco and Other Drugs); 2019 CA Health Education Framework

standards.H-4.1.1.N: Identify the key nutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water) and their functions.
standards.H-4.1.2.N: Describe the food groups and the recommended daily amounts from each (MyPlate).
standards.H-4.1.3.N: Explain the benefits of eating a healthy breakfast and a variety of fruits and vegetables.
standards.H-4.1.4.N: Explain the importance of drinking water and limiting sugar-sweetened beverages.
standards.H-4.1.5.N: Describe the benefits of daily physical activity and the recommended 60 minutes per day for children.
standards.H-4.1.6.N: Explain safe food handling and storage practices.
standards.H-4.2.1.N: Describe internal and external influences (family, culture, media, advertising) on food choices and physical activity.
standards.H-4.3.1.N: Use the Nutrition Facts label to locate valid information about foods.
standards.H-4.4.1.N: Practice effective communication to ask for healthy food and activity options at home and in the community.
standards.H-4.5.1.N: Use a decision-making process to choose healthy foods and snacks.
standards.H-4.6.1.N: Set a short-term goal to improve nutrition or increase physical activity and track progress.
standards.H-4.7.1.N: Plan a nutritious meal and snack using MyPlate.
standards.H-4.7.2.N: Track daily food intake and physical activity.
standards.H-4.8.1.N: Encourage others to make healthy food and physical activity choices.
standards.H-4.1.1.A: Identify safe and unsafe uses of medicines; distinguish prescription and over-the-counter medicines.
standards.H-4.1.2.A: Describe the short- and long-term effects of tobacco and nicotine use, including e-cigarettes/vaping and secondhand smoke.
standards.H-4.1.3.A: Describe the short- and long-term effects of alcohol use.
standards.H-4.1.4.A: Recognize that most young people do not use alcohol, tobacco or other drugs (social norms).
standards.H-4.1.5.A: Identify dangers of inhalants and household poisons.
standards.H-4.2.1.A: Analyze how advertising and the media influence decisions about alcohol, tobacco and other drugs.
standards.H-4.2.2.A: Describe how family and peers influence choices about alcohol, tobacco and other drugs.
standards.H-4.3.1.A: Identify trusted adults and community resources for help with alcohol, tobacco and other drug concerns.
standards.H-4.4.1.A: Demonstrate refusal skills to avoid alcohol, tobacco and other drugs.
standards.H-4.5.1.A: Use a decision-making process to avoid alcohol, tobacco and other drug use.
standards.H-4.6.1.A: Set a personal goal to remain alcohol-, tobacco- and drug-free.
standards.H-4.7.1.A: Practice safe use of medicines (read labels, take only with adult supervision).
standards.H-4.8.1.A: Encourage others to be alcohol-, tobacco- and drug-free.

units.title: Health Skills and Wellness
units.big_idea: Good health comes from everyday choices and skills we can practice.

units.title: Nutrients and MyPlate
units.big_idea: Our bodies need a variety of nutrients from every food group.

units.title: Food Labels and Influences
units.big_idea: Labels give reliable information, while ads and habits influence what we choose.

units.title: Planning Healthy Meals and Food Safety
units.big_idea: Balanced meals and safe food handling keep families healthy.

units.title: Physical Activity for Life
units.big_idea: Sixty minutes of daily activity strengthens the heart, muscles and mind.

units.title: Medicines and Household Safety
units.big_idea: Medicines help when used correctly; unsafe use and poisons can harm.

units.title: Tobacco and Vaping
units.big_idea: Nicotine is addictive and harms the body; most young people choose not to use it.

units.title: Alcohol
units.big_idea: Alcohol affects the brain and body and is especially harmful to growing kids.

units.title: Influences, Decisions and Refusal Skills
units.big_idea: Recognizing influences and practicing refusal skills helps us stay drug-free.

units.title: Health Promotion Campaign
units.big_idea: We can encourage our families and communities to make healthy choices.

objectives: Describe physical, mental and social health

days.title: Health triangle
days.work: Draw a health triangle (physical, mental/emotional, social) and list 3 habits for each side.

days.title: Habit inventory
days.work: Complete a 15-item checklist of daily habits (sleep, water, activity, fruits and vegetables) and circle strengths.

days.title: Health journal
days.work: Set up a health journal and write about one healthy habit your family already has.

days.title: Healthy day schedule
days.work: Plan an ideal healthy day schedule with meals, activity, screen time and 9-12 hours of sleep.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Share the health triangle with family and answer 5 quick-check questions on health dimensions.

days.title: Decision steps
days.work: Learn a decision model (Stop, Think of options, Consider consequences, Choose, Check) and apply it to a snack choice.

days.title: Scenario practice
days.work: Work through 3 scenarios (skipping breakfast, choosing an after-school activity, drink at a party) with the model.

days.title: SMART goals
days.work: Rewrite 4 vague goals ('eat better') as SMART goals.

days.title: Your goal
days.work: Write a personal 2-week SMART goal for eating or activity and make a tracking chart.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain your decision-making steps to a parent using a real choice from today.

days.title: Trusted adults
days.work: Make a 'helping hand' tracing listing 5 trusted adults and how to reach them.

days.title: Reliable vs unreliable
days.work: Compare a health ad with a KidsHealth article and list clues that show which is reliable.

days.title: Asking for help
days.work: Role-play asking a trusted adult for help with a health question.

days.title: Health helpers
days.work: Identify community health helpers (school nurse, pharmacist, doctor, poison control 1-800-222-1222).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a quiz on reliable sources and trusted adults; check your goal tracker.

days.title: Nutrient jobs
days.work: Learn what carbohydrates, proteins and fats do and make a 3-column chart.

days.title: Food sort
days.work: Sort 20 food pictures or packages by their main macronutrient.

days.title: Whole grains
days.work: Compare white and whole-wheat bread labels and explain why whole grains give longer-lasting energy.

days.title: Healthy fats
days.work: Learn the difference between fats in avocados and nuts and fats in fried foods.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz matching carbohydrates, proteins and fats to their jobs and to 10 example foods.

days.title: Vitamins and minerals
days.work: Research one vitamin and one mineral (e.g., vitamin C, calcium) and their sources and jobs.

days.title: Water's job
days.work: Learn how water regulates temperature and track your water intake for one day.

days.title: Sugar in drinks
days.work: Measure the teaspoons of sugar in a soda, juice drink and sports drink using labels and compare.

days.title: Rethink your drink
days.work: Make a chart of 6 healthier drink swaps (sparkling water with fruit instead of soda) with teaspoons of sugar saved.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write 3 reasons water is the best drink choice.

days.title: MyPlate
days.work: Label a paper plate with the 5 MyPlate food groups and recommended proportions.

days.title: Food group collage
days.work: Cut magazine pictures and glue them into the correct food groups.

days.title: Portions
days.work: Measure portion sizes of cereal, milk and fruit and compare to what you usually eat.

days.title: Cultural foods
days.work: Identify food groups in 3 cultural dishes (tamales, stir-fry, pasta).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz naming the five food groups, example foods and the plate proportions for each.

days.title: Breakfast power
days.work: Read about how breakfast fuels the brain and list 5 quick healthy breakfasts.

days.title: Make breakfast
days.work: Prepare a healthy breakfast with 3 food groups.

days.title: Eat the rainbow
days.work: Track the colors of fruits and vegetables you eat for 3 days.

days.title: Taste test
days.work: Taste-test 3 new fruits or vegetables and rate them.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph about the benefits of breakfast and fruits and vegetables.

days.title: Food log day 1
days.work: Record everything you eat and drink today in a food log by food group.

days.title: Food log day 2
days.work: Continue the food log and add activity minutes.

days.title: Food log day 3
days.work: Complete the third day of the food log, including a weekend meal, and total the servings per food group.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Compare your 3-day log to MyPlate and identify one food group to increase.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 2 test on nutrients and MyPlate.

weeks.assessment: Food log analysis and Unit 2 test.

objectives: Locate key information on the Nutrition Facts label
Use % Daily Value to compare foods

days.title: Label parts
days.work: Label a printed Nutrition Facts panel: serving size, calories, fat, sodium, fiber, added sugars and % Daily Value.

days.title: Serving size
days.work: Compare the serving size to the whole package on 3 snacks and calculate how many servings each package holds.

days.title: 5/20 rule
days.work: Learn the 5/20 rule (5% DV or less is low, 20% or more is high) and mark 'low' and 'high' nutrients on 3 labels.

days.title: Pantry scavenger hunt
days.work: Find the cereal or snack in the pantry with the most fiber and the least added sugar and record the numbers.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a label-reading quiz using a new food package.

objectives: Use labels and a decision model to choose snacks

days.title: Whole vs processed
days.work: Compare an apple, applesauce and an apple-flavored fruit snack label and rank them by nutrients.

days.title: Snack decision
days.work: Use the decision model to choose an after-school snack from 4 options and explain the choice.

days.title: Sodium check
days.work: Compare sodium in chips, pretzels, popcorn and nuts and graph the results.

days.title: Make a snack
days.work: Prepare a nutrient-dense snack (veggies and hummus, yogurt parfait) and list its food groups.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a 'Snack Smart' guide with 5 tips and 5 snack ideas.

objectives: Analyze how food ads target kids
materials: recorded TV or online food ads

days.title: Ad detectives
days.work: Watch 3 food commercials and record techniques used (cartoons, prizes, celebrities, catchy songs).

days.title: Cereal box analysis
days.work: Compare the front of a sugary cereal box with its Nutrition Facts label and note what the front leaves out.

days.title: Influences web
days.work: Make a web of influences on your food choices: family, culture, friends, media, cost, taste.

days.title: Create an ad
days.work: Design a cereal box or poster that advertises a healthy food using the same techniques honestly.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph on how ads try to influence kids and how to think critically about them.

days.title: I-messages
days.work: Practice I-messages to ask for healthy food ('I feel more energy when we have fruit at breakfast; could we buy berries?').

days.title: Role-play
days.work: Role-play asking for a healthy option at a restaurant, a friend's house and the grocery store.

days.title: Family traditions
days.work: Interview a family member about a traditional family dish and identify its food groups.

days.title: Healthy twist
days.work: Suggest one healthy twist to the family recipe and discuss it with the cook.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 3 test on labels, influences and communication.

objectives: Plan a balanced meal and snack using MyPlate

days.title: Meal analysis
days.work: Analyze 3 sample dinners and decide which food groups are missing.

days.title: Plan a dinner
days.work: Plan a family dinner that includes all 5 food groups.

days.title: Budget
days.work: Use a grocery flyer to price the ingredients and stay within a $20 budget.

days.title: Snack plan
days.work: Plan two healthy snacks for the week, each combining two food groups (apple with peanut butter, carrots with hummus).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present the menu to family and explain how it follows MyPlate.

days.title: Kitchen safety
days.work: Learn kitchen safety rules (handwashing, knife safety with adult, hot surfaces).

days.title: Shop
days.work: Help shop for the meal planned last week, reading labels to choose items.

days.title: Prep
days.work: Wash produce under running water and, with adult supervision, practice safe cutting with a claw grip.

days.title: Cook
days.work: Cook the planned dinner with an adult and measure ingredients.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a reflection: what food groups were in the meal and how did it taste?

objectives: Explain safe food handling and storage

days.title: Clean
days.work: Use glitter on hands to model germ spread, then practice 20-second handwashing.

days.title: Separate
days.work: Learn why raw meat stays separate from produce and sort grocery items for safe storage.

days.title: Cook
days.work: Learn safe cooking temperatures and check one with a food thermometer.

days.title: Chill
days.work: Check the refrigerator temperature (40°F or below) and list leftovers rules.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Make a Clean-Separate-Cook-Chill poster for the kitchen.

objectives: Make healthy choices when eating out

days.title: Menu choices
days.work: Read a restaurant kids' menu and choose a balanced meal and drink.

days.title: Portions out
days.work: Compare restaurant portion sizes with MyPlate recommendations.

days.title: Fast food swaps
days.work: Find 3 healthier swaps at a fast-food restaurant using online nutrition info.

days.title: Family meal
days.work: Plan a screen-free family meal with conversation questions.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 4 test on meal planning and food safety.

days.title: Benefits
days.work: List physical, mental and social benefits of physical activity.

days.title: Activity types
days.work: Sort activities into aerobic, muscle-strengthening and bone-strengthening.

days.title: Heart rate
days.work: Measure heart rate before and after 3 minutes of jumping.

days.title: Mood check
days.work: Rate your mood before and after a 15-minute walk.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz on the 60-minute guideline, types of activity and three benefits of being active.

days.title: Activity log
days.work: Log activity minutes for 3 days, labeling each activity as light, moderate or vigorous.

days.title: Screen time log
days.work: Log recreational screen time (TV, games, videos) for the same 3 days with start and end times.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Compare activity to the 60-minute goal and screen time to family limits.

days.title: Swap
days.work: List 5 active alternatives to screen time that work indoors and outdoors and try one today.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph about patterns in your logs and one change you will make next week.

objectives: Set and track a physical-activity goal

days.title: Barriers
days.work: List barriers to being active (weather, time, screens) and a solution for each.

days.title: Set goal
days.work: Write a 3-week SMART activity goal (e.g., 30 minutes of outdoor play after school 5 days a week).

days.title: Activity menu
days.work: Create an 'activity menu' of indoor and outdoor choices for rainy and sunny days.

days.title: Track
days.work: Begin tracking the goal on a calendar with stickers and note how you feel each day.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Check progress after 5 days and adjust the plan if needed.

days.title: Family challenge
days.work: Design a one-week family activity challenge with daily tasks (walk after dinner, dance party).

days.title: Lead activity
days.work: Lead the family in a 15-minute active game you choose.

days.title: Advocacy poster
days.work: Make a poster encouraging 60 minutes of play a day for kids in your neighborhood.

days.title: Goal check
days.work: Review your 3-week goal tracker and reflect on progress.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 5 test on the benefits, types and recommended amount of physical activity and on goal setting.

days.title: Why medicines?
days.work: List reasons people take medicines (treat illness, prevent disease, relieve pain) and the risks of misuse.

days.title: Rx vs OTC
days.work: Compare a prescription label and an OTC drug facts label in a Venn diagram.

days.title: Health helpers
days.work: Learn the roles of doctors and pharmacists; write 3 questions you could ask a pharmacist.

days.title: Not candy
days.work: Discuss why some medicines look like candy and why only adults should give medicine.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on types of medicines and who can give them.

objectives: Read medicine labels for safe use
materials: OTC medicine box (empty or with adult)

days.title: Drug Facts label
days.work: With an adult, find active ingredient, uses, warnings, directions and expiration date on a Drug Facts label.

days.title: Side effects
days.work: Learn what side effects are and why you tell an adult if you feel unwell after medicine.

days.title: Safe rules
days.work: Write 5 safe medicine rules (only from a trusted adult, never share prescriptions, follow dose).

days.title: Scenario practice
days.work: Act out what to do if a friend offers you a pill or you find medicine on the floor.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Create a safe medicine checklist and explain it to a younger sibling or parent.

days.title: Poison hunt
days.work: With an adult, find 10 household products with warning labels and note signal words (Caution, Warning, Danger).

days.title: Inhalants
days.work: Learn why sniffing fumes from products like markers, glue or aerosols harms the brain and can be deadly.

days.title: Safe storage
days.work: Help organize cleaning products out of reach and away from food.

days.title: Poison Control
days.work: Learn the Poison Control number (1-800-222-1222) and role-play calling it.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 6 test on medicines and household safety.

objectives: Describe short- and long-term effects of tobacco

days.title: What's in tobacco
days.work: Learn about nicotine, tar and carbon monoxide and what each does to the body.

days.title: Lung model
days.work: Model healthy vs smoker's lungs by soaking one sponge in dark syrup and comparing.

days.title: Straw breathing
days.work: Jog in place, then breathe through a straw for 30 seconds to feel restricted breathing (stop if dizzy).

days.title: Addiction
days.work: Read how nicotine causes addiction and why quitting is hard.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw a body diagram labeling 6 effects of tobacco.

days.title: What is vaping?
days.work: Read an FDA fact sheet on e-cigarettes and list what is in the aerosol.

days.title: Myth or fact
days.work: Sort 10 statements about vaping into myth or fact.

days.title: Flavors and marketing
days.work: Analyze how flavors and colorful packaging target young people.

days.title: Brain effects
days.work: Learn how nicotine affects the developing brain.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a public service message correcting one vaping myth.

objectives: Recognize that most youth do not use tobacco

days.title: Secondhand smoke
days.work: Learn how secondhand smoke and vape aerosol affect others, especially children.

days.title: Smoke-free laws
days.work: Read about California's smoke-free laws for restaurants, parks and cars with kids.

days.title: Social norms data
days.work: Read survey data showing most California students have never used tobacco and graph it.

days.title: Avoiding smoke
days.work: Role-play 3 polite ways to avoid secondhand smoke or vape aerosol (move away, ask to open a window, tell a trusted adult).

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 7 test on effects of tobacco, vaping and secondhand smoke and on social norms.

objectives: Describe short- and long-term effects of alcohol

days.title: What is alcohol
days.work: Learn what alcohol is and why it's illegal for people under 21.

days.title: Short-term effects
days.work: List short-term effects (slowed reaction time, poor balance, poor judgment).

days.title: Coordination demo
days.work: Walk a tape line while spinning first to feel how impaired balance makes tasks hard; discuss.

days.title: Long-term effects
days.work: Learn long-term effects on liver, heart and brain.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Label a body outline with 6 short- and long-term effects of alcohol on the brain, liver, heart and stomach.

objectives: Explain why alcohol is more harmful to young people

days.title: Brain parts
days.work: Label brain parts and their jobs (thinking, memory, balance).

days.title: Growing brain
days.work: Read why young brains are more affected by alcohol.

days.title: Norms
days.work: Read data showing most young people don't drink alcohol.

days.title: Safety
days.work: Discuss drunk driving and what to do if an adult who has been drinking offers you a ride.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write 3 reasons kids choose not to drink alcohol, using facts from this week's readings.

weeks.topic: Family rules and influences about alcohol

days.title: Family interview
days.work: Interview a parent about family rules on alcohol, tobacco and medicine and why they exist.

days.title: Influences
days.work: List positive and negative influences from family, friends and media.

days.title: Trusted adults
days.work: Review trusted adults you can talk to about alcohol or drug concerns.

days.title: Family agreement
days.work: Write a family agreement about staying alcohol- and drug-free.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 8 test on alcohol's effects, social norms and family influences.

objectives: Analyze ads and media messages about alcohol and tobacco

days.title: Ad analysis
days.work: Analyze 3 alcohol or tobacco ads for target audience and hidden messages.

days.title: Movies and TV
days.work: Notice how alcohol or smoking is portrayed in a TV show or movie scene and whether consequences are shown.

days.title: Counter-ad
days.work: Create a counter-ad that shows the truth about a product.

days.title: Social media
days.work: Discuss influencers and sponsored posts that promote vaping.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a media literacy checklist for evaluating ads.

days.title: Types of pressure
days.work: Learn spoken, unspoken, positive and negative peer pressure with examples.

days.title: Scenario sort
days.work: Sort 10 scenario cards by type of pressure (spoken, unspoken, positive, negative) and explain two choices.

days.title: Good friends
days.work: Make a list of qualities of friends who support healthy choices.

days.title: Positive pressure
days.work: Plan a way to use positive peer pressure to encourage a healthy habit.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write about a time you resisted pressure or helped someone else.

days.title: Assertive voice
days.work: Compare passive, aggressive and assertive responses and practice an assertive voice and body language.

days.title: Refusal steps
days.work: Learn refusal strategies: say no clearly, give a reason, suggest an alternative, walk away.

days.title: Role-play 1
days.work: Role-play refusing a vape offered by an older kid.

days.title: Role-play 2
days.work: Role-play refusing alcohol at a party and leaving with help from a trusted adult.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Demonstrate refusal skills in a new scenario for a parent who scores the steps.

days.title: Decision model
days.work: Apply the decision model to 3 ATOD scenarios and write consequences.

days.title: Healthy alternatives
days.work: List 10 healthy activities to have fun and manage stress.

days.title: Pledge
days.work: Write a personal pledge to stay alcohol-, tobacco- and drug-free, with one action you will take to keep it.

days.title: Share
days.work: Share your pledge with a trusted adult and discuss support.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 9 test on influences, refusal and decisions.

objectives: Choose a health message and audience

days.title: Choose topic
days.work: Choose a topic: drink water, eat the rainbow, be active, or stay vape-free.

days.title: Audience
days.work: Identify the audience (family, neighbors, younger kids) and what message will reach them.

days.title: Facts
days.work: Gather 5 facts from reliable sources for the campaign.

days.title: Plan products
days.work: Plan 2 campaign products (poster, short video, flyer, skit).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Get feedback from a parent on the campaign plan.

days.title: Slogan
days.work: Write a catchy slogan and a one-sentence key message for the campaign and test it on a family member.

days.title: Poster
days.work: Create a campaign poster with the slogan, three facts with sources and a clear visual.

days.title: Video or skit
days.work: Record a 1-minute public service video or rehearse a short skit that models the healthy behavior.

days.title: Fact check
days.work: Fact-check every statistic and claim against KidsHealth, MyPlate, FDA or NIDA and correct any errors.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Show the materials to two people, collect one suggestion from each, and revise the poster and video.

weeks.topic: Presenting the campaign and year review

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the campaign to family or a community group.

days.title: Display
days.work: Display posters in a visible place (with permission).

days.title: Year review
days.work: Review nutrition, activity and ATOD key ideas with a game.

days.title: Final assessment
days.work: Take the end-of-year health assessment covering nutrition, physical activity, medicines, tobacco and alcohol.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a reflection on your health goals and set a goal for summer.
